facts.fact: US programmatic digital audio ad spend reached $1.85 billion USD in 2024, up 15.7% YoY and representing 26% of the total market (per eMarketer, cited by StackAdapt).

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article states that there are four main types of programmatic deals advertisers use to facilitate transactions: RTB, private marketplace, programmatic guaranteed, and preferred deals.
facts.quote: there are four main types of deals that advertisers use for facilitating transactions

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article lists seven major benefits of programmatic advertising.
facts.quote: Here are seven of the [major benefits of programmatic advertising]

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article says that in campaign setup, advertisers use a DSP to set targeting criteria and budget for a programmatic campaign.
facts.quote: use a DSP to create and manage the ad campaign, setting the targeting criteria and budget

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article states that the ad selection and display process in programmatic advertising happens within a fraction of a second, faster than the page can fully load.
facts.quote: all within a fraction of a second—faster than the page can even fully load

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article states that in real-time bidding, the highest bidder wins the ad placement and that the winning bid determines the final cost of the ad.
facts.quote: with the highest bidder winning the ad placement (and ultimately determining the final cost of the ad based on the amount of competition involved)

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that it is consistently ranked the #1 demand-side platform (DSP) by G2, a peer-to-peer review site.
facts.quote: StackAdapt is consistently ranked [the #1 DSP](https://www.g2.com/categories/demand-side-platform-dsp) by G2.

facts.fact: The page defines click-through rate (CTR) as the number of clicks divided by the number of impressions, multiplied by 100.
facts.quote: It’s calculated by dividing the number of clicks by the number of impressions and multiplying by 100.

facts.fact: The page defines cost per acquisition (CPA) as total campaign spend divided by the number of conversions attributed to the campaign.
facts.quote: The total campaign spend gets divided by the number of conversions attributed to the campaign to calculate the CPA

facts.fact: The page defines cost per completed view (CPCV) as total campaign spend divided by the number of completed views.
facts.quote: It’s calculated by dividing the total campaign spend by the number of completed views.

facts.fact: The page defines an impression as counted each time a creative is loaded on a webpage, app, or screen and displayed to a user.
facts.quote: An impression is counted each time a creative is loaded on a webpage, app, or screen and displayed to a user.

facts.fact: The page says programmatic advertising can serve ads on thousands of different websites, apps, and streaming services.
facts.quote: serving ads on thousands of different websites, apps, and streaming services

facts.fact: The page defines a conversion as a user completing a specific tracked action, such as a purchase, demo booking, or newsletter signup, after interacting with an ad.
facts.quote: A conversion occurs when a user completes a specific action you’re tracking—for example, making a purchase, booking a demo, or signing up for a newsletter—after interacting with your ad

facts.fact: Programmatic advertising is defined as a subset of digital advertising that uses automated technology and data-driven algorithms to buy and place ads in real-time, often across multiple platforms.
facts.quote: Programmatic advertising is a subset of digital advertising that uses automated technology and data-driven algorithms to buy and place ads in real-time, often across multiple platforms.

facts.fact: Digital advertising, per StackAdapt's blog, encompasses all forms of online advertising, including display, social media, and search engine marketing.
facts.quote: Digital advertising encompasses all forms of online advertising, including display, social media, and search engine marketing.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that programmatic advertising is called programmatic because the ad buying process is automated.
facts.quote: It’s called programmatic because the ad buying process is automated.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's own vendor page says its StackAdapt Academy offers free programmatic advertising courses and certifications.
facts.quote: enroll in free programmatic advertising courses and certifications.
